shortDescription: Fervo Energy NASDAQ:FRVO finished up 26.1% on Monday after declaring commercial operation at Cape Station Phase 1 GeoBlock 1 on September 30, ahead of its contractual commercial operation date, and the 33 MW GeoBlock 1 is operating in line with expectations for production and power delivered under…

children: at Cape Station Phase 1 GeoBlock 1 on September 30, ahead of its contractual commercial operation date, and the 33 MW GeoBlock 1 is operating in line with expectations for production and power delivered under its power purchase agreement.

The company also said GeoBlock 2 has achieved grid sync and is in its early operations phase, delivering test energy to the grid, while GeoBlock 3 is mechanically complete and in cold commissioning; both blocks remain on schedule and are expected to achieve commercial operation by January 1, 2027, which would complete Cape Station Phase 1.

said its agreement with Google—a 15-year, grid-connected, take-or-pay contract for 396 MW across eight GeoBlocks—represents the largest enhanced geothermal power purchase agreement signed to date; first power is expected from these GeoBlocks in mid-2028, with full capacity in operation targeted by year-end 2028.
With the signing of the Google agreement, Fervo
said it now has 1,054 MW of capacity under binding power purchase agreements, representing ~$11.9B in contracted revenue, compared to 658 MW and ~$7.2B in backlog at the end of Q2.

The company also reduced estimated H2 capital spending to $700M-$750M from its previous guidance of $850M-$900M by shifting spending closer to revenue generation without delaying delivery, improving near-term cash preservation while leaving the $2.2B Google-project investment unchanged.

title: Fervo Energy soars as Cape Station's first GeoBlock enters commercial operation
